b: The Minimalists talk about feeling trapped, handcuffs that look like golden bracelets, everyday objects that create visual clutter, the hardest part of decluttering, and much more.
Discontent is a fictional story about a false lack.
Autumn feels trapped in her career, which offers financial security, housing, healthcare, and education benefits but little autonomy or meaning.
What in your life looked like a golden bracelet but turned out to be a pair of handcuffs?
Spend an evening with Joshua Fields Millburn.
Courtney explains how visible text on packaging, labels, and everyday objects can contribute to visual clutter, even in an otherwise minimalist home.
How did Peter Rollins get his black eye?
Cassie wants to know how to make birthdays and holidays feel special without exchanging gifts, especially when society equates celebration with consumption.
After several major life changes and personal losses, Bridget has lost interest in her lifelong hobby but continues accumulating supplies.
Bonnie asks why we desire the desires of others.
Sam argues that minimalist aesthetics often signal wealth and privilege, while clutter can reflect financial insecurity.
Laura, a mother of four, reflects on the emotional challenges of decluttering 500 possessions.
Joshua’s new favorite documentary, plus love song that perfectly illustrates how hope can become its own form of golden handcuffs.
Joshua, Ryan, and T.K.’s pithy, shareable, less-than-140-character responses. Find more quotes from The Minimalists at MinimalMaxims.com.
Discontent is a fictional story about a false lack.
Security becomes a prison when we’re unwilling to leave it.
You’ll never be the hero of your own story if you’re unwilling to become the villain in someone else’s.
Your job is something you do, not someone you are.
Not all clutter takes up physical space.
The purpose of a celebration is connection, not consumption.
You don’t have to preserve your past to honor it.
Clutter is the physical manifestation of an emotional attachment.
You can’t undo a bad purchase by keeping it.
